sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Docker interview questions cover the container runtime every backend engineer is expected to know — image layers and caching, Dockerfile best practices, multi-stage builds, the difference between ENTRYPOINT and CMD, networking modes, volumes and bind mounts, image security (non-root, distroless), and the Spring Boot-specific patterns (layered jars, jib). For orchestration, see the Kubernetes page.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Docker = **process isolation** via Linux namespaces + cgroups.

- **Image** = layered FS + manifest.
- **Container** = running instance + writable top layer.
- **Multi-stage builds** — separate build deps from runtime image.
- **Non-root** by default; **distroless** as the modern best practice.
- **`ENTRYPOINT` vs `CMD`** — entrypoint = executable, cmd = default args.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Docker compose** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Docker fundamentals** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Docker networking** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Docker security** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Multi stage builds** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Layer order** matters — least-frequently-changed first.
- **`.dockerignore`** — both build speed and image-size win.
- **`HEALTHCHECK`** — declared in Dockerfile, surfaced by orchestrator.
- **Spring Boot layered jars / jib** — JVM-aware tooling.
- **Don't run `latest`** — pin tags, prefer immutable digest references.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd build a multi-stage Dockerfile, base on distroless, run as non-root, declare a `HEALTHCHECK`, leverage Spring Boot layered jars for cache hits, and pin the digest in production manifests."*
